newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan rupee ends lower on dollar build-up.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan rupee ends lower on dollar build-up.

text.p: Building up of dollar positions pushed the Sri Lankan rupee lower to end at 55.87 to the U.S. unit on Thursday after opening at 55.83, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 55.80 on Wednesday.
"Early import covering demand fizzled out to be replaced by speculation," said a foreign bank dealer.
Speculation drove the dollar to a high of 55.93 before profit-taking pulled it back, he said.
Overnight call money closed at 13.5 percent, against its opening level of 14, spurring banks to build up their dollar positions, dealers said.

"The dollar is gaining overseas which means the Central Bank will respond positively," a local dealer said, referring to the central bank's practice of reflecing overseas movements when fixing its own selling and buying rates for the dollar.
"Call money is easing to prompt dealers to buy dollars," he said.
